chapter: Porgy and Bess and Varsity Show
title: Gershwin rehearsing him privately at home
summary: Gershwin coached him personally on Ain't Necessarily So and the boat song, since he and Buck could not read music.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Did George Gershwin come to rehearsals?

No. No. He don't come to rehearsals. In fact I forgot to tell you the part, in my part of 'It Ain't Necessarily So,' he rehearsed me in his private home. He rehearsed me personally. It is the oldest piano in his house.

He wanted to help me out with it, help me get it like he wanted it to sound. So he went through it with me, you know? He didn't leave me to do what I wanted to do in song, he rehearsed the song with me himself, "Ain't Necessarily So" and the boat song as well. All the music I was supposed to do, he helped do it with me.
Did he do this with any of the other actors?
No, uh-uh. They all could read music and that was left to -- what's her name -- Eva Jessy, she had the choir, Eva Jessy's choir.
So you couldn't read the music?
No, neither could Buck read the music.
